public_rationale: DeepSeek’s December 2, 2025 report describes knowledge, token-efficiency and complex-task deficits alongside reasoning performance comparable to GPT-5 [e1]. These disclosures challenge categorical parity but do not establish the size of a practical advantage under comparable conditions [e1]. Epoch’s January 2, 2026 analysis reports a US capability lead over a broader period beginning in 2023; it does not isolate December 1–13, 2025 [e2]. Neither source separates the effect of shared scaling methods from resource and implementation differences, so the causal claim remains unresolved [e1, e2].
limitations: DeepSeek’s findings are a developer self-assessment, without comparable measurements establishing the practical magnitude of the disclosed deficits [e1].
Epoch’s broader historical comparison cannot settle the specified December 1–13 window [e2].
The packet establishes neither broad practical parity nor whether shared scaling methods cause an absence of meaningful advantages [e1, e2].

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Because everybody is following the same playbook of ever more massive data and servers fed into ever-larger large language models, nobody has a real technical advantage in the generative AI race.

statement.excerpt: Importantly, since everybody is following the same playbook—ever more massive data, ever more massive servers, fed into ever-larger large language models—nobody has a real technical advantage here.
statement.document_title: The core misconception that is driving American AI policy

from_speaker: everybody is following the same playbook
nobody has a real technical advantage here
our_interpretation: Everybody refers to leading US and Chinese generative AI developers in the surrounding discussion.
The ordinary reading of a real technical advantage is a meaningful practical advantage in capability or computational efficiency, rather than a small difference on one test.
The claim also asserts that shared reliance on scaling explains the absence of such advantages.

The surrounding right-now language describes the state immediately before publication. Use December 1–13, 2025 as the latest partial-month reporting window for public model evaluations, without admitting later model releases.
Do not add a requirement that an advantage last for years; the quoted claim supplies no such duration.
criteria.support_condition: Comparable contemporary evaluations show broad practical parity, technical records establish the stated common approach, and evidence connects that shared approach to the absence of meaningful advantages.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Comparable contemporary evidence establishes a meaningful capability or efficiency advantage despite the shared approach, or directly undermines the claimed causal explanation.

evidence.locator: Section 5, Conclusion, Limitation, and Future Work
evidence.explanation: DeepSeek acknowledges a capability gap and attributes it to training resources, which weighs against an unqualified absence of technical advantages. The same section reports reasoning performance comparable to GPT-5, so it does not establish uniform superiority across tasks.

Epoch reports a persistent US lead under its capabilities index, which challenges broad claims of parity. This aggregate extends beyond the target period and does not isolate the causal effect of a shared scaling approach.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Comparable capability and efficiency evaluations for models available during December 1–13, 2025, with model versions, settings, inference budgets and uncertainty documented, plus controlled comparisons or other credible evidence separating shared scaling methods from resources and implementation differences.
